batchName: Middle Republic: Hannibal in Italy (241-216 BCE) - Medium Batch 1
chapterName: Middle Republic: Hannibal in Italy (241-216 BCE)

questions.question: What did the Ebro Treaty of 226 BC establish?
options: The Ebro as the northern limit of Carthage's sphere
Carthage's right to settle Cisalpine Gaul
The return of Sardinia to Carthage
The Ebro as Rome's frontier in Italy
Joint Roman-Carthaginian rule of Saguntum
questions.explanation: The treaty made the Ebro, a river in north-east Spain, the northern limit of Carthage's sphere. Rome's later deal with Saguntum, south of the river, would cause trouble.
questions.sourceQuote: In 226 BC Rome and Carthage agreed the Ebro Treaty, which made the Ebro, a river in north-east Spain, the northern limit of Carthage's sphere.

questions.question: Who led the Roman embassy that delivered Rome's demands to Carthage after Saguntum fell?
options: Cato the Elder
Fabius Maximus
Claudius Marcellus
Varro
Scipio Africanus
questions.explanation: Fabius Maximus, later famous as Rome's most patient general, led the embassy. Its curt demands were rejected, and Rome declared war in spring 218 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: Rome sent an embassy to Carthage led by Fabius Maximus, the senator later famous as Rome's most patient general.

questions.question: What desperate religious act followed Cannae after priests consulted the Sibylline Books?
options: A new temple was built to Carthage's gods
People were buried alive in Rome's cattle market
The consul Varro was sacrificed to Mars
The Vestal Virgins were exiled from Rome
All temples were closed for a year
questions.explanation: People were buried alive in the cattle market as a sacrifice. The Sibylline Books were sacred prophecies kept for emergencies.
questions.sourceQuote: Priests consulted the Sibylline Books (*Libri Sibyllini*), sacred prophecies kept for emergencies, and people were buried alive in Rome's cattle market as a sacrifice.

questions.question: What did the 'Fabian strategy' involve?
options: Seeking one decisive battle as quickly as possible
Avoiding pitched battles and cutting supply lines
Bribing the Gauls to abandon Hannibal
Fortifying Rome and abandoning the countryside
Invading Africa to force Hannibal home
questions.explanation: Fabius harassed the invaders and cut their supplies while Rome rebuilt its strength. The strategy was deeply unpopular while Hannibal plundered Italy's farmland.
questions.sourceQuote: He avoided pitched battles, harassed the invaders and cut their supply lines, wearing them down while Rome rebuilt its strength.

questions.question: Why were the Celtic tribes of Cisalpine Gaul angry with Rome in 218 BC?
options: Rome had banned their Druid priests
Rome demanded heavy tribute in silver
Rome had enslaved their Iberian allies
Rome was drafting their men into its legions
Rome was founding settler colonies on their best land
questions.explanation: Rome was planting colonies of settlers on the best land of the Po valley. Hannibal's envoys were already courting the angry Gauls.
questions.sourceQuote: Meanwhile, in Cisalpine Gaul (*Gallia Cisalpina*), the Po valley lands of Celtic tribes in northern Italy, Rome was founding new colonies (*coloniae*) of settlers on the best land.

questions.question: From which base did Hannibal begin his march to Italy in 218 BC?
options: Massalia, modern Marseille
Gades, modern Cádiz
New Carthage, modern Cartagena
Saguntum, on Spain's east coast
Carthage, in modern Tunisia
questions.explanation: New Carthage, now Cartagena, was Hannibal's main base. He marched north from it in May or June 218 BC.
questions.sourceQuote: In May or June 218 BC he marched north from New Carthage, his main base, now Cartagena.

questions.question: How did Carthage cope with its war debt to Rome after the First Punic War?
options: It paid by surrendering its fleet
It paid it with ease
It took fifty years to pay
The Ebro Treaty cancelled it
It defaulted and was invaded
questions.explanation: Carthage remained the most prosperous port of its day and paid the debt easily. The Barca family soon began planning how to stand up to Rome again.
questions.sourceQuote: It remained the most prosperous port of its day and paid its war debt to Rome with ease.

questions.question: Against whom did Carthage fight the Truceless War after 241 BC?
options: Iberian tribes south of the Ebro
The Celtic tribes of the Po valley
The Roman legions in Sicily
Its own rebellious mercenaries and African subjects
Greek colonists from Massalia
questions.explanation: Carthage was fighting for its life against its own mercenaries and African subjects. Rome used the distraction to seize Sardinia and Corsica.
questions.sourceQuote: Carthage was soon fighting for its life against its own rebellious mercenaries and African subjects, a struggle known as the Truceless War.

questions.question: How large was the army Rome raised to confront Hannibal at Cannae?
options: About 150,000 men
About 86,000 men
About 40,000 men
About 26,000 men
About 60,000 men
questions.explanation: Eight Roman legions plus as many allied troops made about 86,000 men, the biggest army Rome had ever raised. The Romans packed their infantry unusually deep.
questions.sourceQuote: The Senate (*senatus*) answered with the biggest army Rome had ever raised: eight Roman legions (*legiones*) plus as many allies, about 86,000 men.

questions.question: Why did Rome's agreement with Saguntum alarm Carthage?
options: Saguntum had sheltered Carthage's rebel mercenaries
Saguntum lay north of the Ebro, in Rome's sphere
Saguntum was Carthage's main silver port
Saguntum lay well south of the Ebro, in Carthage's sphere
Saguntum controlled the Alpine passes
questions.explanation: Saguntum lay well south of the Ebro, so Carthage saw the agreement as Roman meddling in its own sphere. The city later stood alone against Hannibal's conquests.
questions.sourceQuote: Some time after the Ebro Treaty, Rome made a separate agreement with Saguntum, a city on Spain's east coast lying well south of the river.
